page-title.purpose: The h1 on Papers, Projects, People and Articles: one or two words, the largest type on the site.

display.purpose: The home hero headline, two-tone, at most 21ch.

headline.purpose: Section and chapter heads, two-tone, at most 24ch.

title.purpose: Paper titles, project tiles, card and outreach titles.

lede.purpose: The paragraph opposite a page title and each chapter's hook, in ink-2, at most 46ch.

body.purpose: Reading text; prose at most 68ch, abstracts and captions 70ch.

small.purpose: Captions, meta rows, venues and the search field.

label.purpose: Uppercase list headings in ink-3 (sidebar groups, footer columns); never above a headline.

data.purpose: Counts, years, bit strings, the placeholder tag and labels drawn inside figures; tabular figures.

shadows.name: toast
shadows.purpose: The confirmation toast at the bottom of the screen.

shadows.name: lightbox
shadows.purpose: An enlarged photo over an 88% near-black scrim.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The house exponential ease-out for every state change, reveal and expansion.

motion.name: duration-state
motion.purpose: Color, border and opacity changes on links, buttons, chips.

motion.name: duration-ui
motion.purpose: Chevron and arrow nudges (.3s), the mobile menu (.25s fade, .35s slide), search width (.4s), abstract expand (.5s).

motion.name: duration-zoom
motion.purpose: Hover zoom of faces (.5s, 1.03x), gallery photos (.6s, 1.04x), card media (.7s, 1.035x) and portraits (.7s, 1.03x).

motion.name: power-on
motion.purpose: A figure's wipe and scan line each time it starts playing on hover; the live layer fades back to the still over .35s.

motion.name: view-transition
motion.value: out .18s ease; in .38s house ease with a 10px rise
motion.purpose: Cross-document page transitions; the header holds still. Theme switches and paper filtering also run inside a view transition.

motion.name: caption-pop
motion.purpose: Live captions inside figures, timed to the event they explain.

motion.name: loop
motion.purpose: Animation loop length; seamless, or faded over the last and first half second.

breakpoints.name: restack-small (faculty, footer, mission intro, code card)
figure-compact (figure width; animations drop secondary labels)

narrative.overview:
The NET Lab site is the research-lab category standard played straight, at the polish of MIT Media Lab and Google DeepMind. Its North Star is a great paper figure come alive: a quiet, nearly monochrome page is the gallery wall, and every paper and project hangs on it as a rounded stage running a live animation of its own mechanism. The page recedes so the work can lead. Color and motion live in the figures, not in the chrome.

The voice is precise, calm and quietly playful. One self-hosted grotesk carries every word, set heavy and tight in two-tone headlines whose gray second half does the job an eyebrow or kicker would do elsewhere. Red Hat Mono appears only where the machinery shows: counts, years, figure labels and the placeholder tag. Landing surfaces are generous and airy; the archive pages are long, orderly runs of entries between hairlines.

The logo's seven trace colors are the research areas, one color per area, everywhere. The home page opens calmly: a plain statement of what the lab does beside the logo, so a visitor who has never heard of the lab understands it first. Motion has one grammar, exponential ease-out, and it is asked for, never imposed: every figure rests on a chosen still frame, and only the one being hovered (or focused, or on a phone the one in the middle of the screen) wipes in behind a scan line in its area color and plays; pages cross-fade through view transitions; visitors who prefer reduced motion only ever see the stills. The aim is smooth and beautiful, never overstimulating. Confirmed rejections: the Bootstrap card stack the old site used, the plexus or mesh background every networking lab ships, costume worlds of any kind, a busy animated hero (the lab's PI found the first one confusing for newcomers), per-figure pause buttons, and copy that recites counts ("7 projects, 23 papers").
keyCharacteristics: Near-white and near-black grounds, cool gray inks, 1px hairline rules.
Seven logo colors, each meaning one research area and nothing else.
Two-tone grotesk headlines (ink, then gray); no eyebrows or kickers.
Every paper and project explained by a live figure on a 16px rounded stage.
Neutral pill controls; a selected state inverts to ink.
Red Hat Mono for data and machine text only.
Flat surfaces; shadow only for what floats.
Exponential ease-out; figures rest on a still and play on hover, no scroll reveals.

rules.name: The One Meaning Rule
rules.body: Each logo color means one research area, everywhere. Color enters a component only through its `data-area` attribute: `--area` for fills, strokes, dots and hover underlines, `--area-ink` for text. Anything without a research area stays neutral. Three exceptions only: the logo itself; the home page's press links, which cycle through the seven colors in area order so each hover underline differs, like the project tiles above them (the PI asked for this); and transient interaction cues (the focus ring, text selection, the caret).

rules.name: The Ink Variant Rule
rules.body: No text is ever set in a base logo color. Area text uses its -ink variant, which clears AA on every ground in both themes. Every base color fails AA as text in at least one theme: six of the seven on the light ground (Chartreuse at 1.4:1), Plum on the dark.

rules.name: The Neutral Chrome Rule
rules.body: Navigation, buttons, chips, inputs and rules are drawn in ink and gray only. A selected chip inverts to ink; it never fills with an area color. An area appears in a control only as its dot.

rules.name: The Two-Tone Rule
rules.body: A headline that continues past its claim does so in gray (ink-3) in the same run, as in "We make wireless networks do more than they were built for." with "than they were built for." gray. Most section heads are just the claim ("Latest papers"). Nothing sits above a headline: no eyebrow, kicker or overline.

rules.name: The Mono Is Data Rule
rules.body: Red Hat Mono is for data and machine text: numbers, years, bit strings, figure labels and captions, the placeholder tag, shell commands. Headlines, body copy, buttons and navigation stay in the grotesk.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Structure is drawn with 1px rules in Hairline, never with boxes and shadows. Paper entries, press links, sidebar lists, publications, principles and footer rows are open rows between hairlines. Shadow is reserved for what floats: the toast and the lightbox.

rules.name: The Stage Rule
rules.body: What you look at sits on a 16px rounded stage that clips it; what you press is a full pill. Media never floats on the page without its stage.

rules.name: The Contribution Rule
rules.body: In every animation the lab's contribution (the hidden channel, the new mechanism, the key result) is drawn in the area color, and everything else (the world, baseline systems, axes, infrastructure) is neutral figure ink. A diagram uses one logo color: its area's.

rules.name: The Hover-To-Play Rule
rules.body: A figure moves only while someone is looking at it on purpose, and announces itself each time with the wipe and scan. Nothing on a page moves on its own: no autoplaying figures, no scroll-triggered reveals, no fade-ups, no staggered entrances.

rules.name: The Placeholder Honesty Rule
rules.body: A figure whose animation runs on sample data wears the dashed "Suggested animation · replace me" tag until its item is marked final. A tag comes off when its author marks the item final, and any that remain come off together at launch through the one site setting; never by restyling the tag or hiding it in CSS.

dos: Do color by research area only, through `data-area`: `--area` for fills, strokes, dots and hover underlines, `--area-ink` for text.
Do write headlines in two tones: the claim in ink, the continuation in ink-3 in the same run.
Do put every animation, photo and portrait on a 16px rounded stage that clips it, and make every control a full pill (999px).
Do separate list entries with 1px hairlines and leave the rows open.
Do draw the lab's contribution in the area color and everything else in neutral figure ink, with weight (strokes of 2px and up, filled marks) and an area-ink label.
Do keep the "Suggested animation · replace me" tag on every figure until its item is marked `animation_status: final`, and remove the rest at launch with `show_placeholder_markers: false`.

Do move with the house ease, cubic-bezier(.16, 1, .3, 1): .2s for color and border changes, .3–.5s for chevrons, menus and expanding panels, .5–.7s for image zooms, 1s for a figure's wipe, .35s for its fade back to the still.
Do give every animation a `still` moment and honor reduced motion everywhere: no wipe, no view transitions, no animated zooms, no blinking caret.
Do set text inside figures in fig-ink-2 or stronger, and area text in its -ink variant.
donts: Don't use a logo color for decoration or for anything that is not a research area: not a page, a header, a button, a principle, a person or a cover. The press links' hover underlines are the one sanctioned exception.
Don't set text in a base logo color; each one fails AA as text in at least one theme.
Don't put an eyebrow, kicker or overline above a headline. Small uppercase labels head lists (sidebar groups, footer columns) and panels inside figures, nothing else.
Don't put shadows on cards, figures or rows. Shadow belongs to the toast and the lightbox.
Don't set headlines, body copy, buttons or navigation in Red Hat Mono.
Don't add a decorative plexus, mesh or node-network background, or go back to a bordered card stack; node-link drawings appear only when they plot real data.
Don't add scroll reveals (fade-ups, staggered entrances) or autoplaying motion; a figure plays only while hovered.
Don't paint a background in a diagram (the stage supplies it), and don't put anything essential under the tag (top-left 250×46).
Don't animate the home hero or fill it with traces, pulses, puzzles or tag bars; it says what the lab does, plainly.
Don't add pause or play buttons to figures; nothing plays unless someone hovers.
Don't recite counts in headlines and ledes ("7 projects", "23 papers", "9 students"); counts belong in filter chips and result lines.
Don't go lighter than fig-ink-3 for any text inside a figure; it is the AA floor on both stages.
